title: Grilled Salmon
description:
We had never heard of this dish until Wegman’s arrived in State College and offered this ready to go in the seafood department.
What a treat and it couldn’t be much easier to make, either pre-packaged from Wegman’s or if you do the set up yourself. The only hard part is getting the wood slab to cook on. You can’t just go to the local lumber yard; you need specially treated hickory. Fortunately, Wegman’s now carries packages of the wood planks and I’m sure there are other sources from the internet.
And, you need to plan ahead a little in order to soak the board for 30 minutes or so before cooking (or you’ll have a big fire in your grill).
ingredients: 4 salmon filets, about ½ pound each or a 2 pound filet
1-4 hickory planks, depending on the size
First, soak the wooden plank in water for 30 minutes or so.
Rub the four salmon filets with a little olive oil. (If you start with one large filet, cut into four pieces.)
directions: After combining the Monterey steak seasoning and the brown sugar, gently rub the mixture all over the salmon.
Squeeze a little lemon juice over the filets.
About 10 minutes before you’re ready to cook, turn the grill on high.
When ready, put the rubbed salmon on the plank and put the plank on the grill.

With the grill on medium-high and the lid closed, grill for 7-10 minutes, depending on the thickness of the filets and how much on the rare or cooked side you like salmon (usually a little pink in the center is much better).
You’ll get some smoke coming out and you should check now and then to make sure the board is not burning up. If it begins to char too much, spray a little water on the edges.
Carefully slide the filets off the plank with a spatula and serve.
You can also make a quick salsa, like this Mango Salsa, which is a delicious complement to the smokiness of the salmon.
Combine all the ingredients above and mix well, but gently.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
